title: Returning Closures
goal: Return a closure from a function by transferring captured values.

sections.text: You return closures from functions just like any other value, but one scope rule changes how captures work.

sections.caption: impl Fn describes the return type.

sections.text: Local variables die when a function returns. A returning closure cannot borrow variables from that function's scope.
Adding `move` forces the closure to take ownership of its captured variables. The captured values live inside the closure as long as the closure exists.

sections.code:
let add_five = make_adder(5);
let result = add_five(10);
sections.caption: add_five owns its captured n.

sections.text: If you omit `move`, the compiler complains that the closure outlives the local scope with error `E0373`.

explanation: Return a closure from a function by transferring captured values.
